input.subject: Loose pipe in back garden – Flat 7, 87 Alder Lane (R/PM028-1)
input.body:
Good morning,

Re: Flat 7, 87 Alder Lane, Bellmere, ZZ3 8ZZ – loose pipe in the back garden (ref R/PM028-1).

Your landlord has let us know they will arrange the repair themselves, so they or their contractor may contact you directly to arrange access. We will check in with you in about a week to see whether it has been sorted.

In the meantime, please avoid putting any strain on the pipe. If it starts leaking water and you cannot contain it, turn off the water at the stopcock if it is safe to do so and contact us straight away.

Kind regards
Donna
Northbridge Lettings

data.reasoning:
Since the landlord is arranging this independently, there's no need to reply to them directly. I'm thinking through how to handle the approval status — "rejected" here just means the agency wasn't instructed to proceed, not that the request itself failed. I'll note that clearly, inform the tenant, log the fact, and decide whether to hold the ticket in place or close it out, since no contractor is coming through the agency.

For safety, I'll keep it on hold to confirm resolution with the tenant rather than closing outright. Since the tenant has no email on file, I'll check whether send_message can still reach them another way.

result.summary: The landlord, Grace Oakley, replied "We will sort this issue." This answers the agency's question: she will arrange her own contractor, so she doesn't need a reply. I recorded the pending approval as declined (the agency won't instruct a contractor, but the repair itself isn't refused) and noted that she is arranging this repair herself. I also told the tenant what happens next, with safety advice, and placed a 7-day hold to check the repair has been done.

The tenant was last told in event 004 that we were waiting for the landlord, so they need an update.
